prompt:
Create one full-fidelity desktop website comp for The Lobby’s Privacy page, landscape 3:2, edge to edge, crisp readable text, no browser surround. This short public document explains information use and the choices available to visitors and members.

Lead with “Privacy” and “How The Lobby uses information when you visit, sign in, and use its Tools.” Then “Visiting” with “The Schedule Downloader is open without signing in.”

The central composition is quiet paired reading rows under “What we keep” and “What you control”, with clear common row alignment and generous prose measure, separated by fine navy rules, not individual cards. Use these three rows:
“Signing in” — “We keep your email address, Tool access, and a sign-in session so you can return to your Tools. The sign-in cookie lasts up to 90 days and renews while you use the site.” Paired with “Leaving The Lobby” — “Removing membership deletes the access record and Remembered teams.”
“Remembered teams” — “Members can save teams and use a replaceable private calendar link.” Paired with “Your choices” — “You can replace your Member link.”
“Connecting Google Calendar” — “Google asks for permission to view and edit events across your calendars. The Lobby changes only events it adds in the calendar you choose.” Paired with “Disconnecting” — “Disconnecting removes upcoming games The Lobby added; played games stay.”

Finish with “Running the site” — “AWS and Cloudflare help run and protect The Lobby. Basic service logs and counts of calendar use help keep it working.”

Compact masthead “The Lobby”, ordinary “Back to The Lobby” link, quiet footer with tiny decorative reference robot. Reference supplies navy linework, Rubik headings and Nunito Sans prose. Use pale seafoam reading ground. Exclude greeting hero, buttons, scenery, grain, dates and invented claims.
approvalScope: Privacy design brief and paired reading layout confirmed; implementation and publication have not been requested.
